sources.citation: ISO 639-3 documentation page for [kve] Kalabakan; Universiti Malaysia Sabah eprints search 'Murut Kalabakan' (43 hits); Crossref query 'Kalabakan Murut language' (20 hits); DOAJ query; archive.org text search
sources.note: No grammar, phonology, thesis or article on Kalabakan Murut surfaced: UMS hits are Murut sociolinguistics at Keningau (Tagal/Timugon area); Crossref hits are history/ethnography; DOAJ's single hit is the Glossa paper above; archive.org holds only Wikipedia stub dumps and no Rosetta Project record for kve.

sources.note: Nothing. Historical account of PMur *-b/*-d/*-g > MKal -m/-n/-ŋ via fricativization, 'based on Blust 2016' (a talk handout). a full-text search for stress/accent/penult/prosody: 0 hits apart from a reference title.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2018. Two birds with one stone: the aerodynamic voicing constraint and the languages of Borneo. JSEALS 11(2): 1-18 (hdl 10524/52424). Table 6 'Voiced coda nasalization in Kalabakan Murut of southeast Sabah', pp. 8-9, data 'as recorded by Jason Lobel'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Kalabakan stress; the paper's stress remarks (penultimate stress, stressed schwa) concern Bario Kelabit only. Kalabakan section is a table of Proto-Murutic > KM final-nasalization reflexes with affixed forms (e.g. a-nakum / takub-on).

sources.note: Nothing; no phonology section on either page.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (ScholarSpace hdl 10125/101972). Sec. 4.3.6 and Table 4.47 Murut Kalabakan pronouns (pp. 147-148); Table 5.11 Tidung Kalabakan verb system; fn. 7 p. 215 on *R.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Kalabakan or any Murutic language. Every stress/accent/penult hit in the dissertation concerns Philippine languages (Bikol, Manide/Inagta Alabat 8.2.9 'Contrastive accent', Maranao, Subanen, Umiray Dumaget). Murut Kalabakan data are pronouns and sound correspondences; forms carry no accent marks.
